summary: Well-executed, preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic network verifier plus one automated repair iteration into an LLM intent→configuration pipeline. The authors archive a complete preregistration, execution manifest, raw artifacts, and analysis. On a deterministic synthetic task corpus (N=500) and with a shared-initial-generation design, baseline proposals passed the verifier 499/500 and guarded (verify→repair) passed 500/500, yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0,0.006]); McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. The manuscript is reproducible and frank about scope and limitations, but a few clarifications are required to avoid misinterpretation of what the experiment measures and to resolve minor accounting ambiguities in the archived manifest.
critical_issues: The manuscript does not yet make sufficiently explicit that the experimental design uses a single shared initial LLM proposal per task (generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate') and therefore measures the verifier+repair effect conditional on that candidate rather than the effect of verifier-guided regeneration. This is a substantive interpretive limitation that must be stated clearly in the Abstract, Methods (preregistration reference), and Discussion to prevent readers from inferring that the verifier produced changes via iterative regeneration.

The execution-accounting labels in the manifest are potentially confusing (e.g., provider audit condition_counts reported as {shared:500, guarded:1} while guarded_success_count=500). The manuscript must reconcile and explain these accounting fields (shared initial generation vs. repair-stage calls) and show, with artifact references, how model_calls_used=501 maps to baseline and guarded outcomes so that readers can verify that the single repair call corrected the single baseline failure.

The statistical reporting is technically correct but requires a brief explicit statement (Methods or Results) explaining why the exact McNemar two-sided p-value equals 1.00 in the presence of a single discordant pair (n10=1, n01=0) and what that implies for interpretation under a ceiling-effect regime. This avoids misreading the non-significant p as evidence that verifiers are unnecessary.
required_revisions: Add explicit, unambiguous wording in the Abstract, Methods, and Discussion that the study used a single shared initial generation per task and therefore estimates verifier+repair impact conditional on that same candidate rather than measuring verifier-in-the-loop regeneration. Cite the preregistration artifact (SHA-256) and the execution_manifest paths that define generation_semantics to support the claim.

Add a short subsection or paragraph that reconciles model-call accounting: (a) show the mapping from shared_initial_generation/repair/provider-call-stage counts to baseline and guarded condition outcomes, (b) explain why condition_counts may show guarded:1 while guarded_success_count=500 (i.e., that the guarded arm re-used the shared candidate and only invoked the repair-stage provider call once), and (c) point to the exact artifact paths/hashes (e.g., execution/model_configuration.json, execution/provider_calls/*, execution/scoring/*.json) that verify these facts.

Add one or two sentences in Methods/Results explicitly explaining the exact McNemar p-value behavior given n10=1,n01=0 and noting that the result reflects a ceiling effect and severely limited discordant-pair count; include (or reference) the paired-bootstrap CI method and parameters already archived to support the CI claim.
optional_revisions: Report (in an appendix or short paragraph) exploratory per-cluster summaries (VLAN/ACL/static-route) from archived artifacts to give readers a sense of distributional variation; label these as exploratory per the preregistration.

Add a brief forward-looking paragraph clarifying how an alternative design that permits verifier-feedback-guided regeneration would address different operational questions, and reference the relevant artifacts showing the current design choice.

Clarify in the Disclosure the precise path and hash for the initial master prompt (master_prompt.txt SHA-256) in the body near the existing Disclosure sentence that references it, to make discovery slightly easier for readers verifying autonomy claims.
